body: Forgot to mention I'm on Windows 11 pro

Before starting, for anyone that download the MRP's, as the OP stated, the bug only happens with `Forward+`, but the second one (46_blockbenchimport_test - Copy.zip) was configured with `Mobile` renderer, so be sure to change this before testing. Also, the first one don't crash because uses `Vulkan` as driver and if my testing is correct, the bug only happens with `D3D12`.
My PC: ``` Godot v4.7.dev (583596cd5) - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated Intel(R) Arc(TM) B580 Graphics (Intel Corporation; 32.0.101.8735) - AMD Ryzen 5 3600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 31.91 GiB memory - WASAPI (48000 Hz, Stereo/mono) ```
I did some tests and the result i get was: - The bug only happens with the combination of `D3D12`, `Forward+` and the models inside the MRP - The FBX was the model that i feel more easier to trigger the bug, especially the `Locker` object - I was able to reproduce down to 4.4 stable, 4.7 dev 5 and latest master - I was able to trigger the bug moving the camera, moving the model and clicking on the `Locker` object (shown on video 2) - On my tests, what happens is somehow the MRP trigger a device removal - After the bug starts, 2 things can happen: - The 3D area of the editor freezes, some parts of the editor renders pure black, move the mouse the mouse around the editor throw errors and some actions crash the editor, like hover the mouse somewhere to show a tooltip, (Most common on 4.6.2 and lower) - The editor totally freezes with a wave of error spam that doesn't stop until you kill the process (Most common on 4.7 versions)
Using the VSCode to run Godot, when the bug starts, a lot of messages (i guess comes from windows) starts to show and for last, 2 errors from D3D12: ``` D3D12: Removing Device. D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12Device::RemoveDevice: Device removal has been triggered for the following reason (DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG: The Device took an unreasonable amount of time to execute its commands, or the hardware crashed/hung. As a result, the TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) mechanism has been triggered. The current Device Context was executing commands when the hang occurred. The application may want to respawn and fallback to less aggressive use of the display hardware). [ EXECUTION ERROR #232: DEVICE_REMOVAL_PROCESS_AT_FAULT] D3D12 ERROR: ID3D12CommandQueue::ExecuteCommandLists: Command lists must be closed before execution. [ EXECUTION ERROR #837: EXECUTECOMMANDLISTS_OPENCOMMANDLIST] ``` The amount of text are quite big, so i'll upload a .txt file instead: [Msg + D3D12 errors.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27030682/Msg.%2B.D3D12.errors.txt)
After this, when you move the mouse or when the editor freezes, these errors are spammed:
Errors ``` ERROR: Parameter "vertex_array" is null. at: RenderingDevice::draw_list_bind_vertex_array (E:\Godot Dev\Godot Fork\servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:4819) ERROR: The vertex format used to create the pipeline does not match the vertex format bound. at: RenderingDevice::draw_list_draw (E:\Godot Dev\Godot Fork\servers/rendering/rendering_device.cpp:5005) ERROR: Condition "!(((HRESULT)(res)) >= 0)" is true. ye, thats an Intel driver bug. The Intel GPU hang is caused by divergent forward_clustered shaders. The divergence is caused by alpha channel in textures and alpha_scissor_threshold.

If you configure alpha_scissor_threshold in the mesh surface texture to be 0.0,  then no discard is applied resulting in non divergent shaders. 
WARNING!!! Changing texture transparency setting caused my gpu to hang indefinitely)
